The development must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date hereof.Reason: To comply with Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990, as amended.

No demolition or development shall take place until an updated Demolition and Construction Logistics and Management Plan (CLMP) has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority in consultation with Transport for London (TfL). The CLMP shall include details of: (a) loading and unloading of plant and materials; (b) storage of plant and materials; (c) programme of works & measures for traffic management (including routing) so as to minimise the impacts of construction traffic on the highway; (d) means to prevent deposition of mud or other substances on the highway; (e) provision of  boundary hoardings, behind any visibility zones of construction traffic routing; (f) hours of operation; (g) means to control dust and emissions to air incorporating recommendations of the Air Quality Assessment; (h) means to control noise and vibration. The CLMP should be in accordance with the Greater London Authority's Supplementary Planning Guidance 'Control of Dust and Emissions during Demolition and Construction'. The approved CLMP shall be adhered to throughout the construction period.Reason: To ensure that the proposed development does not interfere with the free flow of traffic and conditions of safety on the public highway, does not have a significant adverse impact on the amenities of nearby residential properties and to minimise the impacts on local air quality and complies with Policies 29, 34 and 36 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018. Reason for pre-commencement: This condition is required to be pre-commencement as the CLMP needs to be in place before any works take place and to mitigate against the impacts of the construction process. Given the location of the development on major roads and bus routes, the construction phase needs to be carefully managed to avoid congestion, obstruction, harmful impact and disturbance.

Prior to commencement of the development hereby permitted a Construction Environmental Management Plan (CEMP) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, based on the recommendations within the submitted Preliminary Ecological Appraisal (Greengage, January 2025).The CEMP shall be in accordance with BS42020:2013 and include the following:a) the qualifications, role and responsibilities of the appointed on site Ecological Clerk of Works (ECoW) or similarly competent person;b) pre-demolition nesting bird strategy, including surveying, prevention of nesting and licensed removal, as necessary to allow demolition to proceed;c) measures to prevent entrapment of mammals in open pits / trenches;d) construction lighting to ensure it is in accordance with Guidance Note 08/18 Bats and artificial lighting in the UK Bats and the Built Environment series by the Institute of Lighting Professionals and the Bat Conservation Trust (especially towards the nearby SINC)All works carried out during the construction period shall be undertaken in accordance with the approved CEMP.Reason: To enhance and protect the biodiversity value of the land in accordance with Policy 26 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018. Reason for pre-commencement: This condition is required to be pre-commencement to ensure that protected species and the biodiversity value of the adjacent SINC (St. Nicholas Churchyard) are not harmed or, are adequately mitigated for, prior to the demolition / construction process.

No development (with the exception of above ground demolition works) approved by this planning permission shall commence until a remediation strategy to deal with the risks associated with contamination of the site in respect of the development hereby permitted, has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority. This strategy will include the following components: 1.  A site investigation scheme to provide information for a detailed assessment of the risk to all receptors that may be affected, including those off site.2.  The results of the site investigation and the detailed risk assessment referred to in (1) and, based on these, an options appraisal and remediation strategy giving full details of the remediation measures required and how they are to be undertaken.3. A verification plan providing details of the data that will be collected in order to demonstrate that the works set out in the remediation strategy in (2) are complete and identifying any requirements for longer-term monitoring of pollutant linkages, maintenance and arrangements for contingency action.Any changes to these components require the written consent of the Local Planning Authority. The scheme shall be implemented as approved.Reason: To ensure that the site does not pose any further risk to human health and does not contribute to, and is not put at unacceptable risk from or adversely affected by, unacceptable levels of water pollution in accordance with Policy 34 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.Reason for pre-commencement: This condition is required pre-commencement as it relates to how contamination will be investigated and remediated during construction and then during operation.

Prior to the superstructure works of the development hereby permitted, details of the type and treatment of the materials, including samples, to be used on the exterior of the buildings shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Such details shall include means of enclosure to the all ground level commercial units, roller shutter doors, screens, doors and fenestration. 1:20 or 1:50 scale elevation drawings shall also be submitted showing the proposed use of the materials in elevational treatment of the development hereby approved. The approved materials shall be used in the construction of the development hereby approved, completed prior to its occupation/use and retained thereafter.Reason: To safeguard the visual amenities of the area and to ensure compliance with Policy 28 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

With the exemption of demolition, site preparation and drainage, development shall not commence unless and until details of all land levels and finished floor levels have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. There shall be no change in levels unless specifically shown on the approved plans.Reason: To safeguard the visual amenities of the area and to ensure compliance with Policy 28 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Prior to commencement of the development hereby permitted, a scheme for habitat creation shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. This will take the form of a Biodiversity Enhancement and Management Plan (BEMP) in general accordance with BS42020:2013, to provide the highest possible Net Gain value on site, which in turn will contribute to nature's recovery in the wider landscape. The BEMP will provide:a) a Biodiversity Net Gain evaluation of the development, working to the a statutory methodology and include post-development Condition Assessment sheets;b) Green infrastructure, including but not limited to:a) Extensive substrate based biodiverse roofs / biosolar roofs / blue roofs (including how access for management will be created and maintained),b) Various terraced gardens / intensive green roofs with planting for people and wildlife,c) living walls / fences / screens,d) hanging baskets / balcony planting of value to biodiversity,e) culinary herb planters for residents / commercial usage,f) planter seating,g) rain gardens, planted SuDS, bioswales etc. in the 'public realm' areasThese will be provided to maximise local biodiversity and contribute to increased urban permeability. Full details on substrate (including physico-chemical information), species, planting density and abundance will be provided, including cross-sectional views. Biodiverse / biosolar roofs must utilise solely native species. Green infrastructure should select species appropriate for the type of roof / planting proposed, in accordance with Clause c.c) A soft landscaping masterplan will detail biodiversity enhancement through planting schemes that provide nectar, pollen and fruit resources throughout the seasons, a variety of structural diversity and larval food plants, through no less than 60% native and local species by number and diversity. Substrate, provenance and numbers of all bulbs, seeds and plugs / whips / trees will be detailed, as will aftercare and ongoing management. Ornamental plants will not include any genera or species on Schedule 9 of the Wildlife and Countryside Act (1981) or the LISI list and should be on the "RHS Plants for Pollinators" lists (or of documented wildlife value), to provide increased resource availability;d) A timetable of delivery for each habitat to be created (month and year);e) Details on the monitoring of habitats and the provision of a monitoring report, including BNG calculations, which shall be provided to the LPA on the 1st November of each year of monitoring (years 1-3 after creation, years 5, 7 & 10 and every 5 years thereafter until year 30), which will assess the condition of all habitats created and any and all necessary management or replacement / remediation measures required to deliver the Net Gain values set out in clause a) for each habitat;f) Details of the contingency methods for management and funding, should the monitoring identify changes are required to ensure the habitat(s) are in the appropriate condition to deliver the Net Gain values set out in the BEMP for each habitat.g) A short 'resident booklet' on how all Green Infrastructure, soft landscaping and features for wildlife have been installed to make the building as wildlife friendly as possible, to improve their access and understanding of wildlifeWork shall be undertaken in accordance with the approved scheme and thereafter retained in perpetuity.Reason: To enhance biodiversity in accordance with Policy 26 of the Sutton Local Plan2018.Reason for pre-commencement: This condition is required to be pre-commencement to ensure that the post-development biodiversity value of the land is fully assessed prior to the demolition / construction process.

No roof mounted equipment (including roof plant, vents, lift runs, aerials, satellite dishes, solar panels) may be installed unless and until precise details of this equipment have been submitted to and agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Details shall include the following:- The exact location of the equipment on the roof;- The height of the equipment above the roof;- The materials and finish of the equipment;- Drawings to demonstrate the visual impact of the equipment from St Nicholas Way, St Nicholas Road, and adjacent High Street; andDemonstration from the siting of the equipment that all practical measures have been adopted to minimise the visual impact of the equipment on the surrounding area.The development shall be implemented and maintained strictly in accordance with the agreed details. No additional roof equipment shall be added to or altered without the prior written agreement of the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To enable the Local Planning Authority to control the development in detail in the interests of visual amenity by endeavouring to achieve buildings of visual quality in accordance with Policy 28 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Prior to rising above the damp proof course of the development hereby permitted, a scheme for wildlife and nesting features shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. These will be include:a) Exposed south-facing sand piles for solitary bees (on biodiverse / biosolar roofs) and solitary bee bricks / posts at all levels (south facing);b) Deadwood loggeries (at roof levels);c) Preformed ponds (can be integrated within biodiverse roofs);d) Features on buildings, in accord with the adopted Biodiversity Strategy, including at least:i) 12no. integrated multi-chamber swift bricks,ii) 2no. black redstart boxes,iii) 12no. integrated bat roosts, if these can be protected from light pollution,iv) 1no. peregrine falcon nesting box / scrapeThe scheme will include full details on: numbers of each feature, type of feature / box / brick, location (plan and elevation views) of each feature, height above ground (if applicable) and nearest external lighting (if bat boxes are deemed feasible).Features shall be undertaken in accordance with the approved scheme and thereafter retained in perpetuity.Reason: To enhance the biodiversity value of the land in accordance with Policy 26 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Within six months of commencement of the development, a BREEAM New Construction V6.1 Design Stage Certificate, issued by the Building Research Establishment (BRE) or equivalent authorising body, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority to show that an 'Excellent' rating will be achieved and that the score targeted in the pre-assessment has been met or exceeded.Reason: To comply with Policy 31 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

With the exemption of demolition, site preparation, and drainage, development shall not commence until further details of the proposed communal air source heat pump (ASHP) system have been submitted and approved in writing by to the Local Planning Authority, including:(i) the sizing, positioning and orientation of the proposed ASHP units;(ii) product specifications and an estimate of the heating and/or cooling energy the ASHP system would provide to the development and the electricity required for this purpose;(iii) the expected heat source temperature and the heat distribution system temperature;(vi) confirmation of the CO2 emissions savings expected to be achieved.Reason: To comply with London Plan Policies SI2, SI3 and SI4, and with Policy 31 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

With the exemption of demolition, site preparation, and drainage,  development shall not commence until full details of the overheating strategy accompanied by an updated TM52 Thermal Analysis Report have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The updated Thermal Analysis Report must demonstrate that all co-living units will achieve compliance with the relevant TM52 overheating criteria using the DSY1 weather file for London. The proposed development shall be constructed in accordance with the approved overheating strategy.Reason: To comply with Policy 31 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

With the exemption of demolition, site preparation, and drainage, development shall not commence until documentary evidence has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority to show that the development will achieve an improved Green Space Factor (GSF) score of at least +0.2 compared to the baseline GSF score prior to redevelopment. The Council's GSF scoring system set out in the Council's 'Technical Guidance Note - Building a Sustainable Sutton' (June 2018) must be used for this purpose. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details and thereafter retained.Reason: To comply with Policy 33 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

With the exemption of demolition, site preparation, and drainage, development shall not commence until a report has been carried out by a competent acoustic consultant that assesses the likely noise impacts from the development of the ventilation/extraction plant, and mitigation measures for the development to reduce these noise impacts to acceptable levels and has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The report shall include all calculations and baseline data and be set out so that the Local Planning Authority can fully audit the report and critically analyse the content and recommendations. The level of noise emitted from any plant hereby approved shall be at least 5dB(A) below the background level, as measured from any point 1 metre outside the window of any room of a neighbouring residential property. If the noise emitted has a distinguishable, discrete continuous note (whine, hiss, screech, hum) and/or distinct impulse (bangs, clicks, clatters, thumps), then it shall be at least 10dB(A) below the background level, as measured from any point 1 metre outside the window of any room of a neighbouring residential property. The measures approved under this condition shall be implemented in their entirety prior to the commencement of the use/first occupation of the development and retained as such thereafter.Reason: To safeguard the amenity the amenity of surrounding occupiers and of future occupiers in accordance with Policies 29 and 34 of Sutton Local Plan 2018.

With the exemption of demolition, site preparation and investigations, development shall not commence until revised drainage calculations that include half drain down time and modelled area details have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. A revised drainage layout must be provided and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority to confirm the invert levels of the proposed discharge point, and the maintenance plan updated to include the maintenance tasks and frequency of all proposed SuDS and confirm a maintenance owner. The system shall be implemented and thereafter managed and maintained in accordance with the approved details.Reason: To prevent the risk of flooding to and from the site in accordance with the London Plan Policy SI 13 and Policy 32 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

The flats shall not be occupied until plans and elevations showing the exact location, materials and details of the wind mitigation measures to the terraces and public realm improvements, and their management, in accordance with the Wind Microclimate Cfd Study prepared by Windtech Consultants and dated January 2025, have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The wind mitigation measures shall be implemented in accordance with the agreed details prior to occupation of the flats and thereafter retained. Reason: To ensure that the amenity of the surrounding occupiers and future occupiers of the development is protected in accordance with Policies 28 and 29 of Sutton Local Plan 2018.

The flats and commercial units hereby permitted shall not be occupied until the refuse and recycling areas have been provided in accordance with the approved plans. The areas shall be maintained as such thereafter. Reason: To ensure the operational requirements of the site can be met and to ensure adequate provision of refuse and recycling facilities in the interest of amenity for future and neighbouring occupiers in accordance with policy 29 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Prior to first occupation of the development hereby permitted, a full Delivery and Servicing Plan (DSP) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority in consultation with Transport for London (TfL) and shall include the following specifications: All deliveries should be timed outside of the peak hours. Details confirming the traffic management for vehicles reversing into the northern passageway, including trained traffic marshals. Details confirming how cargo cycle and powered two-wheeler deliveries will be made safely, limiting impact to the public realm and safe access for pedestrians. The approved details shall be implemented and permanently retained thereafter.Reason: In the interest of road safety and to safeguard the amenity of nearby residential properties in accordance with Policy 29 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

The development shall not be occupied until the proposed modified access to and from the development on St Nicholas Way has been constructed and ready for use by proposed occupiers of the development. All other existing redundant vehicular access points and crossovers to the development shall be permanently closed, be reinstated and returned to a raised kerb prior to first occupation, in a manner to be agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: In the interest of pedestrian and vehicle safety in accordance with Policy 36 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

The development shall not be occupied until space has been laid out within the site in accordance with the approved plans for 3 disabled (blue badge) cars to be provided as shown on the approved plans. The parking area shall be used and permanently retained exclusively for its designated purpose for the life of the development. Reason: To prevent obstruction and inconvenience to other highway users, in the interest of highway safety, and in accordance with Policies 36 and 37 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Prior to first occupation of the development hereby permitted, full details of the 270 long-stay co-living cycle spaces, 10 short-stay co-living cycle spaces, 20 long-stay commercial cycle spaces and 38 short-stay commercial cycle spaces shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority which shall also show the location, size and materials of the provision and the means of access, including compliance with the London Cycling Design Standards. The approved details and numbers of cycle spaces shall be implemented on site prior to the first occupation of the development hereby approved and thereafter permanently retained in accordance with the approved details for the life of the development.Reason: To ensure the development provides an adequate level of cycle parking facilities and to encourage sustainable modes of transport, in accordance with Policies 36 and 37 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Prior to first occupation of the development hereby permitted, a management plan for the communal amenity shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Prior to the first occupation of the co-living units hereby approved, the communal amenity shall be fully implemented and made available for use by future occupiers. The amenity shall be maintained as such thereafter unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To create a high quality environment for future occupiers and to ensure that the provision of communal amenity space is maintained to a high quality in accordance with Policies 9 and 28 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Prior to first occupation of the residential units hereby permitted, full details of the noise attenuation measures installed, including sound transmission reduction measures to be installed between the ground floor commercial units and the first floor co-living units, and guidance on the proper and effective use of the measures to be provided as part of the Welcome Pack to all residential units shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Details regarding any servicing and maintenance must also be included. A copy of the Welcome Pack shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority. The approved details shall thereafter be installed prior to the occupation of the residential units and permanently maintained as such thereafter.Reason: To safeguard the amenity of future occupiers and to ensure that all future residents are aware of the mitigation measures and the proper use of them in accordance with Policies 29 and 34 of Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Prior to the occupation of any of the ground floor units for purposes falling within Class E(b) of the Town and Country (Use Classes) Order 1987 (as amended), details of the proposed extract ventilation system (including the extraction hood, internal fan, flexible couplings, three-stage filtration [grease filters, pre-filters and activated carbon filters]), height of the extract duct above eaves level and anti-vibration mountings shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Particular consideration should be given to the high level discharge of kitchen extract air. The approved details shall thereafter be installed prior to the use of the premises and permanently maintained as such thereafter.Reason: To ensure that the development does not result in odour disturbance to neighbouring residents in accordance with Policies 29 and 34 of Sutton Local Plan 2018.

The development shall not be commenced until details of the 'Secured by Design' measures to be incorporated into the development have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority (in consultation with the Metropolitan Police). The details shall demonstrate how the development incorporates the principles and practices of Secured by Design. Once approved, the development shall be carried out and retained in accordance with the approved details.Reason: In pursuance of the Council's duty under section 17 of the Crime and Disorder Act 1998 to consider crime and disorder implications in exercising its planning functions; to promote the well-being of the area in pursuance of the Council's powers under section 2 of the Local Government Act 2000 and Policy 28 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018. The development should provide a safe and secure environment in accordance with Policy D11 of the London Plan 2021.

Prior to first occupation of the development hereby permitted, evidence (e.g. photographs and installation contracts) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority to demonstrate that the sustainable drainage scheme for the site has been completed in accordance with the approved details. The sustainable drainage scheme shall be managed and maintained thereafter in accordance with the agreed management and maintenance plan for all of the proposed drainage components.Reason: To comply with the London Plan (Policies SI 12 and SI 13) along with associated guidance to these policies and Policy 32 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Prior to first occupation of the development hereby permitted, a final scheme of public realm improvements, including the re-provision of refuse and recycling facilities on the alleyway with High Street to serve the High Street commercial units, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme shall include drawings of a scale of 1:20 showing the street furniture, planters, lighting, paving, and refuse and recycling storage proposed, and shall include materials and maintenance strategy for the paving of the public realm and refuse and recycling storage within the whole redline of the application site. The approved details and refuse and recycling storage shall be implemented in connection with condition of landscape management strategy of this decision notice and shall be retained thereafter for the lifetime of the development.Reason: To ensure that the proposed public realm is of high quality in accordance with Policy 28 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Prior to first occupation of the development hereby permitted, a detailed Landscape Management Strategy shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, which shall include full details of hard and soft landscaping in respect to the communal gardens and roof terraces as well as the public realm and details of on-going soft and hard landscaping maintenance following first occupation and shall also be informed from the Biodiversity Enhancement and Management Plan (BEMP) as conditioned above. The approved Landscape Management Strategy shall be implemented in full. All hard and soft landscaping and tree planting shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details and to a reasonable standard in accordance with the relevant recommendations of appropriate British Standards (in particular, BS 3882: Specifications for Topsoil, Recommendations (2015) and BS 8545: Trees from Nursery to Independence in the Landscape, Recommendations (2014) or other recognised codes of good practice). The works shall be carried out prior to the occupation of any part of the development or in accordance with the timetable agreed with the Local Planning Authority. Any tree(s) or plants that (within a period of five years after planting) are removed, die, or (in the opinion of the Local Planning Authority) are damaged or defective shall be replaced as soon as is reasonably practicable with others of a similar size/species/number as originally approved, unless the Local Planning Authority gives its consent to any variation.Reason: To ensure the provision, establishment and maintenance of a reasonable standard of landscape in accordance with the approved designs in accordance with Policies 26 and 28 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Prior to the installation of any lighting features of the development hereby permitted, a sensitive lighting scheme shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The lighting scheme will include:a) post-development light levels, presented as 1m centre spot values down to 0.1lux, with isolux contour lines showing light degradation and 3D luminance in-the-scene modelling, including into the nearby SINC (St. Nicholas Churchyard) to the west;b) assessment of external lighting and light spill from any buildings through windows / security lighting etc.;c) the technical details of the luminaires and columns to be used, including their location, type, shape, dimensions and expected luminance output and specifically explaining what design attributes have been chosen to minimise light pollution (including timing of lighting, automatic timing switches, PIR sensors etc.);d) vertical spill shown in cross-sectional views focussing on the nearby SINC (St. Nicholas Churchyard) to the west.Lighting will be designed to minimise impacts on biodiversity as outlined in Guidance Note 08/18 Bats and Artificial Lighting in the UK [Bats and the Built Environment series by the Institute of Lighting Professionals and the Bat Conservation Trust].Reason: To protect the biodiversity value of the land and adjacent land, in accordance with Policy 26 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Prior to occupation of the development hereby permitted, a Statement of Conformity shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.The Statement of Conformity will be signed by a Suitably Qualified Ecologist (SQE) and include evidence in the form of full details on:a) starting and completion dates for each created habitat;b) any limitations / impeding factors during each habitat creation phase;c) time stamped photographs of each habitat undergoing creation;d) post completion photographs of each habitat;e) post installation photographs of each habitat, nesting / roosting feature under the above Condition of Features for Wildlifef) proof will be provided that all natural environment data (e.g. habitats, species, green infrastructure features) from ecological surveys for the site (including pre- and post-development), has been or can be shared with Greenspace Information for Greater London CIC (GiGL), London's environmental records centre, following GiGL's data standards.This condition is to certify that the details for each habitat / feature, as approved under the BEMP, are in accord with the submitted information.Reason: To enhance the biodiversity value of the land in accordance with Policy 26 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

12 months post-occupation of the development hereby permitted, a BREEAM New Construction V6.1 Post-Construction Certificate, issued by the Building Research Establishment (BRE) or equivalent authorising body, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority to demonstrate that an 'Excellent' rating has been achieved in accordance with the approved details. All the measures integrated shall be retained for as long as the development is in existence. Reason: To comply with Policy 31 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

The development hereby approved shall be constructed in accordance with the approved Energy Statement (Version 8) (C80 Solutions Ltd, 19 June 2025) together with the approved air source heat pump (ASHP) details. Prior to first occupation of the shared living accommodation, 'as-built' Simplified Building Energy Method (SBEM) and/or Standard Assessment Procedure (SAP) outputs as appropriate shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority to demonstrate that the development has delivered the targeted reduction in carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions compared to the Part L 2021 baseline. All of the approved measures must thereafter be retained for as long as the development is in existence. Reason: To comply with London Plan Policies SI2, SI3 and SI4, and with Policy 31 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Within three months of construction of the development, a finalised 'as-built' Whole Life Carbon Assessment (WLC) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority in order to demonstrate that modelled carbon emissions for each building life-cycle stage meet the targeted Halycon ESG and RIBA 2030 benchmarks for upfront embodied carbon (Module A1-A5) and Whole Life embodied carbon (Module A-C) and improve upon the RIBA Business As Usual (BAU) target for operational. The finalised WLC Assessment must reflect the outcome of the detailed design stage, be prepared in accordance with the Mayor's updated WLC Guidance 2022 and be accompanied by a completed GLA WLC Assessment Template for the Post Construction stage.Reason: In the interests of sustainable development and to maximise on-site carbon dioxide savings in accordance with Policy 31 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018 and London Plan Policy SI2.

The development hereby approved shall be constructed in accordance with the approved Circular Economy Statement prepared by Carbon Climate Certified Ltd (Rev.03) and dated 29 January 2025. Within three months of construction of the development, documentary evidence must be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority which demonstrates that all proposed circular economy measures and the relevant recycling and reuse targets have been met line with the approved details.Reason: In the interests of sustainable waste management and in order to maximise the re-use of materials in accordance with Policy 31 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018 and London Plan Policy SI7

Prior to first occupation of the co-living units hereby approved, documentary evidence must be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority which demonstrates that the overheating strategy has been implemented in line with the approved details.Reason: To comply with London Plan Policies SI4 and Policy 31 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Prior to first occupation of the development hereby permitted, a verification report demonstrating the completion of works set out in the approved remediation strategy and the effectiveness of the remediation shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The report shall include results of sampling and monitoring carried out in accordance with the approved verification plan to demonstrate that the site remediation criteria have been met.Reason: To ensure that the site does not pose any further risk to human health or the water environment by demonstrating that the requirements of the approved verification plan have been met and that remediation of the site is complete in accordance with Policy 34 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

39 number of units (10%) hereby approved shall be designed and constructed in accordance with Building Regulations Part M4 (3) as shown on the approved A3966-ASA-ZZ-XX-SH-A-0700 RevP35 Proposed Schedule of Accommodation as Accessible units. Evidence from an approved building control inspector demonstrating compliance should be submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority prior to the first occupation of the development. The development shall be retained in accordance with these approved details thereafter, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To ensure that the wheelchair units would be capable of providing adequate amenity in accordance with Policy 9 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

No cables, wires, aerials, pipe work, meter boxes, alarm boxes, lighting, satellite dishes, flues, vents or other external fixtures other than those shown on the approved drawings shall be affixed to the exterior walls of the development hereby approved unless precise details have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The fittings shall thereafter be retained in accordance with the agreed details.Reason: To enable the Local Planning Authority to control the development in detail in the interests of visual amenity by endeavouring to achieve buildings of visual quality in accordance with Policy 28 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

The water fittings installed in the residential units hereby approved shall comply with the specifications set out in the submitted section 'Water usage' as contained in the document titled 'Energy & Sustainability Statement' prepared by C80 Solutions and dated January 2025.Reason: To comply with Policy 33 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

In the event of any activity being undertaken within the development site which would fall under Class E(b), (d), and (f) a scheme shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority for the acoustic insulation of the building to ensure that any neighbouring residential and/or commercial occupiers are not adversely affected. The scheme shall be implemented before the E(b) or (d) or (f) use commences and thereafter permanently retained.Reason: To ensure the development is in accordance with policies 29 and 34 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

In the event of any activity being undertaken within the development site which would fall under Class E(a), (b) and (d) these premises shall not be used by the public for the purposes hereby permitted before 8am and after 11pm Monday to Sunday.Reason: To ensure the development is in accordance with policies 29 and 34 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Any works during the demolition / construction phase that generates noise beyond the site boundary shall be only carried out between the hours of 08.00 and 18.00 Mondays to Fridays and between 08.00 and 13.00 on Saturdays and not at all on Bank Holidays and Sundays.Reason: To safeguard the amenity of surrounding occupiers during the construction phase in accordance with Policies 29 and 34 of Sutton Local Plan 2018.

All Non-Road Mobile Machinery (NRMM) of net power of 37kW and up to and including 560kW used during the course of the demolition, site preparation and construction phases shall comply with the emission standards as published on the NRMM Website (https://nrmm.london/). Unless it complies with the standards set out on the website, no NRMM shall be on site, at any time, whether in use or not, without the prior written consent of the Local Planning Authority. The developer shall keep an up to date list of all NRMM used during the demolition, site preparation and construction phases of the development on the online register at https://nrmm.london/.Reason: To safeguard the amenity of surrounding occupiers during the construction phase in accordance with Policies 29 and 34 of Sutton Local Plan 2018.

If, during development, contamination not previously identified is found to be present at the site then no further development (unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority) shall be carried out until a remediation strategy detailing how this contamination will be dealt with has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The remediation strategy shall be implemented as approved.Reason: To ensure that the development does not contribute to, or is not put at unacceptable risk from, or adversely affected by, unacceptable levels of water pollution from previously unidentified contamination sources at the development site in accordance with Policy 34 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

The development must be carried out in accordance with the provisions of the Outline Fire Safety Strategy and Fire Statement Form prepared by Ashton Fire and dated 19 March 2025.Reason: To ensure that the development incorporates the necessary fire safety measures in accordance with the Mayor's London Plan Policy D12.
description: FORMAL DESCRIPTION: Partial demolitions, extensions, refurbishment and change ofuse of existing building to provide new shared living residential accommodation (Sui Generis),flexible commercial floorspace (Class E), flexible commercial and music venue floorspace (Class Eand Sui Generis (music venue and drinking establishment)), amenity space, landscaping, new cycleparking, and other associated works.DETAILED DESCRIPTION: Partial demolitions, part 5, 8 and 15-storey extensions, refurbishmentand change of use of the existing building to provide 359 shared living residential accommodation(co-living units- Sui Generis), flexible commercial floorspace (Class E), flexible commercial andmusic venue floorspace (Class E and Sui Generis (music venue and drinking establishment)),amenity space, landscaping, new cycle parking, and other associated works.
